subject: Which method should I use: stepwiseqtl or MQM model?

messages.author: 49a67c6e0f03dace
messages.subject: Which method should I use: stepwiseqtl or MQM model?
parts:
Hello Everyone!

I'm recently working on a cross population with around 250 individuals of a haploid fungal organism, and I perform QTL analysis with more than 10,000 markers from RADseq data. Previously I performed the analysis according to the r/qtl book by reading in the data as a backcross, and did the multiple QTL analysis manually by using stepwiseqtl to choose multiple QTL model (codes are shown below). Now I would like to try MQM by using mqmscan, because some of my results from stepwiseqtl is quite different from manual scan (showed below). So my questions are:

(1) Can I trust the results from stepwiseqtl, as it sometimes results the same as scene one but sometimes gives me the QTLs that I can't find manually? (I used fitqtl after stepwiseqtl to fit the model, and all the qtls are highly significant).

(2) Can I use MQM to perform the qtl analysis? I'm a bit worried about the large amount of  markers in my data, which could lead to problems for running. 

What would you suggest?

Thanks a lot!



Code:

AllChr <- read.cross("csvr","","test.csv", na.strings=c("-"),genotypes=c("AA","AB"),alleles=c("A","B"),estimate.map=F )
AllChr <- jittermap(AllChr)
AllChr <- calc.genoprob(AllChr, step=1, err=0.001)


out1.bin <- scanone(AllChr, pheno.col=16, method = "hk")
plot(out1.bin)
summary(out1.bin)
qtl1 <- makeqtl(AllChr, chr = 11, pos = 8.39e+01, what="prob") #fix one QTL on chr11
out1.c <- addqtl(AllChr, pheno.col=16, qtl=qtl1, method = "hk")  
summary(out1.c)


... (# repeat above steps and manually adding the QTLs with increasing or decreasing LOD to the model)


qtl5 <- makeqtl(AllChr,chr = c(11,3,1,7,3), pos =c(8.39e+01, 307.1, 621.3, 160.6, 221.2), what="prob") # the QTLs can manually found for this phenotype
out5.c <- addqtl(AllChr, pheno.col=16, qtl=qtl5, method = "hk")  # last scan to confirm no more QTLs with changing LOD above the permutation threshold (scanone with n.perm=1000)
summary(out5.c)


outsw <- stepwiseqtl (AllChrSuperNew1,pheno.col=16, chr =c(11,3,1,7), method = "hk", keeptrace=TRUE)

outsw

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Which method should I use: stepwiseqtl or MQM model?
parts: (1) Can I trust the results from stepwiseqtl, as it sometimes results the same as scene one but sometimes gives me the QTLs that I can't find manually? (I used fitqtl after stepwiseqtl to fit the model, and all the qtls are highly significant).
We can’t say whether the results are trustworthy. Lots of artifacts can arise. But if the results were always the same as scanone(), we wouldn’t ever need to do anything beyond scanone().
(2) Can I use MQM to perform the qtl analysis? I'm a bit worried about the large amount of  markers in my data, which could lead to problems for running.

It’s always worth a try. I think the only potential issue is the amount of missing genotype data.

karl

messages.author: 49a67c6e0f03dace
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Which method should I use: stepwiseqtl or MQM model?
parts:
Thanks a lot Karl for the quick reply!

(1) yeah, you are right that if every result is the same as scanone, then we will not need multiple QTL model anymore. I just want to be a bit cautious about the results I get. :)

(2) For the missing genotype, I use fill.geno, because mqmaugement will end with too large data to run. The actual problem I get is from mqmsetcofactors or mqmautocofactors. Since I have a huge number of markers, I think the cofactor number should also be huge to find the closely linked QTLs (I set around 1000 markers or every 20 markers to select cofactors). But then the analysis ends with an error stating too many cofactors. 

So how many cofactors do you suggest me to set?

Thanks again Karl!

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Which method should I use: stepwiseqtl or MQM model?
parts:
(2) For the missing genotype, I use fill.geno, because mqmaugement will end with too large data to run. The actual problem I get is from mqmsetcofactors or mqmautocofactors. Since I have a huge number of markers, I think the cofactor number should also be huge to find the closely linked QTLs (I set around 1000 markers or every 20 markers to select cofactors). But then the analysis ends with an error stating too many cofactors. 

So how many cofactors do you suggest me to set?

You can't have more cofactors than you have sample size to estimate their coefficients, and I would avoid having more than n/5 parameters in your model, where n is the sample size. But I'd go for maybe 10 at most.

karl
